explanation:
[EFFECT] Temperature has a non-monotonic, arch-shaped effect. Very cold conditions (normalised values near 0.02, roughly 1°C) strongly suppress demand, and the contribution rises steadily as temperatures warm. It peaks around a normalised value of 0.72 (approximately 29–30°C), after which very hot temperatures cause it to fall back and turn negative above roughly 0.90 (≈37°C).
[IMPORTANCE] This is the third-most important feature (rank 3, importance 0.197), carrying roughly the same weight as the year variable just above it.
[RECOMMENDATION] Operational planning should be driven overwhelmingly by the **hour of the day** — staff and bikes should be concentrated around the 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. rush-hour peaks and scaled back sharply overnight — with **temperature** as the key secondary lever, since demand climbs steadily from cold weather up to around 29–30°C and then softens in extreme heat.
